text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- First ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation starts in Singapore with hopes that it will pave the way for freer global trade.
- Singapore's Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says voting for opposition will hurt economic recovery.
- WTO expects world trade growth to speed up again in 1997 after a comparative slowdown in 1996.
- Malaysia Airlines and Thai Airways signal their intent to buy larger Boeing 747s.
- Taiwan to allow stock index futures trading in October 1997.
- Singapore's Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong says biggest challenge of WTO is to get countries to reaffirm commitment to freer trade and fulfil past pledges.
- World equity markets expected to recover after being rattled by US Federal Reserve's chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks that "exuberance" could inflate asset values.
- Taiwan firms, lured by prospect of a Singapore listing, boost their direct investment in Singapore by record 300 percent in first nine months of 1996.
- Car distributor Komoco aims for listing on Singapore bourse.
